venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Monday 7/6 (MOD: MKZ).** Net sales $932 vs a $1,162 target (−20%); food $114; comps $10.60; 26 guests at a $35.84 check average. Weather sunny, 90s with a breeze. Slow, steady shift with a pop at the start — lots of two-tops, it was date night — plus a full bar for the USA vs. Belgium game and some campers at the end of the night. Check averages held in the mid-30s as guests consistently ordered food and a drink or two. Food orders went out well, BOH knocked out cleaning projects and FOH reset to zero from the weekend; closer pushed to an 8pm in-time on low volume, opener out at 8:30. 86: cast iron sour (liquor order arrives tomorrow). No incidents. Favorite moment: seeing a crowd for both soccer games tonight.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Monday 7/6 (MOD: KK; Chef: LSM).** Net sales $1,120 vs a $1,394 target (−20%); food $96; comps $4 / 0.3%; 46 guests at a $24.36 check average. Overcast and warm. A pretty steady Monday — busy at the start with a handful of Meal Deals, a middling lull, then steady again from 9–10:30pm. Cleaned well 3 in preparation for the weekend but did not restock it against time; the chiller once at well 3 (with attached rail-bottle shelf) is now near well 4, a potential sticking point for reopening well 3 Friday — worth exploring options ahead. Decent kitchen sales, smooth service. 86: Champ Lassi. Maintenance: chiller. No incidents. Favorite moment: guests asking for the team's D&D names, which sparked an idea for a one-shot TTRPG theme night.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Monday 7/6 (AM: Carey; PM: Maggie).** Total net sales $6,257.07 vs a $7,303 target (−14%); 140 guests (Tock) at a $44.69 check average; comps $161.10. Splits: DC/AM $715.39, D&C PM $5,541.68; food $1,850.85; net event sales $78 (total incl. events $6,335.07). Slow day, made cuts, then a busy night with a little pop toward the end — shoutout Rachel for help with dishes. Kitchen highlights: lightish prep, 911 on agnolotti/braised baby carrot/lemon aioli/coconut gel, low on succotash/cocktail sauce/mignonette, no 86s. Event: held a High School Success board meeting for 6 guests 8am–2:30pm in suite 6A — a relaxed affair in their 3rd year with us, prepping for three more days of meetings. No incidents.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Monday 7/6 (MOD: Kyler; Chef: Alejandro).** Net sales $3,868 vs a $4,119 target (−6%); beverage $3,152, food $675, retail $40; comps $68.20; 102 guests (Sevenrooms) at a $38 check average. Periodic rain, surprisingly crisp and cool. First turn defined by high-food-ordering tables that kept the floor busy despite only four tables; mellowed before resurging after 10pm, though rain discouraged a lot of parties. Never hit full capacity (rail empty all night) but maintained flow with a kaleidoscope of post-soccer parties. Set a new oyster record: 174 (past 169), plus 102 covers, 1 large party, 6 solos, no investor cocktails. Top sellers: Rosalie, Vodka Shots, Fries. Friendly faces: Matty Clark before the USA–Belgium game, Evan Saez, and D&C LA regular Brent Picha. 1 no-show (charged). Maintenance: pass metal thing is loose. No glassware breakage.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.weather: Good weather, no effect on service
venues.narrative: **LA — Monday 7/6 (MOD: Mikey/Vic; Chef: Jersh).** Net sales $3,569 vs a $4,615 target (−23%); food $770 (all Marquee); comps $146.50 (Griffin & Kendall, a G&L shareholder, employee discount, Yiban, and Vic's friend Yazmin); 95 guests at a $75.94 average. Good weather, no effect. A pretty mellow night without much of an Oyster Monday pop, which made for a chill, easy service — 95 covers who came to occupy space more than to order big, likely early-month rent recovery, maybe bummed by the USA soccer loss. Mostly date-night couples and many first-timers. One table tried to walk out but Angel caught them on the staircase; one cancellation and one resi meant for tomorrow (rebooked). Never started a waitlist; some bigger parties occupied tables 1–3. Easy-going, quick-paced close. Kitchen: slow Oyster Monday (kumamotos slept on); prep should be date-labeled. 86: pot de creme and cookies (oven); low on rockfish. No incidents.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative: **DCDC — Monday 7/6 (MOD: Josh).** Marquee bar sales $2,243.83 vs a $2,776 target (−19%); food $193.60; comps $22 (1%), voids $83 (4.1%); 42 guests at a $39.60 guest-count average. Hot with light thunderstorms; Garden closed. Slow Monday with another day of intense heat — quiet start with mostly two-tops (mix of resos and walk-ins escaping the heat), team stayed productive with ABK projects. Around 8:45pm a nice push filled the bar top and several tables at once; everyone jumped in, comms solid, service smooth through the rush. Cut the host once it settled, last call 11:30pm, wrapped by 12:30am — a decent night considering the heat, slow start, and the USA vs. Belgium match. Kitchen snacks only (note: make cookie dough Fri/Sat for Sun–Mon service). No incidents. Favorite moment: a quick store run for cookies after selling out let a celebrating couple end on a sweet note.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Monday 7/6 (AM: Braden/Jonathan; PM: James/Marcus).** Total net sales $3,264 vs a $4,000 target (−18%); food $1,299; comps $149; ~81 Municipal Bar covers (14 AM / 67 PM, OpenTable) at a $40.30 average. Hot with a quick energetic storm around 7pm (thunder and lightning) that cleared right back up. Splits: Municipal Bar morning $670 / evening $2,395, Sun Club $199, Hot Eye closed. Slow morning off the holiday — Sam crushed it solo into 2pm. Very slow, purposefully short-staffed evening: after ~9pm Sam was the only server with Tanner and Aimee supporting floor and bar; Matt left ~7pm and Jason handled the bar solo easily. Sun Club slow, closed a touch early ahead of the fast-moving storm with no one on the deck. Kitchen: no 86s, no low counts, nothing sent back. A last-minute Joyride booking came in. No incidents. Favorite moment: the team working together to stay ahead of sidework and leave at a reasonable hour despite being so short-staffed.
